audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Cana sign, mother of Jesus, water into wine, first sign/glory, temple action, temple/body saying, and trust/knowing motif.

verses.restored: On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.

familiar.text: And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:

modern.text: On the third day a wedding took place at Cana in Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there,

original.text: Καὶ τῇ ⸂ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ⸃ γάμος ἐγένετο ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας, καὶ ἦν ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἐκεῖ·

verses.restored: Jesus also was invited to the wedding, and his disciples.

familiar.text: And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.

modern.text: and Jesus and His disciples had also been invited to the wedding.

original.text: ἐκλήθη δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν γάμον.

verses.restored: When the wine ran short, the mother of Jesus says to him, They have no wine.

familiar.text: And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.

modern.text: When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to Him, “They have no more wine.”

original.text: καὶ ὑστερήσαντος οἴνου λέγει ἡ μήτηρ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἶνον οὐκ ἔχουσιν.

verses.restored: Jesus says to her, What to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.

modern.text: “Woman, why does this concern us?” Jesus replied. “My hour has not yet come.”

original.text: ⸀καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, γύναι; οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου.

verses.restored: His mother says to the servants, Whatever he says to you, do.

familiar.text: His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.

modern.text: His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever He tells you.”

original.text: λέγει ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ τοῖς διακόνοις· ⸂Ὅ τι⸃ ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε.

verses.restored: There were six stone water jars set there according to the purification of the Judeans, each holding two or three measures.

familiar.text: And there were set there six waterpots of stone, after the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three firkins apiece.

modern.text: Now six stone water jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification. Each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons.

original.text: ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ ⸂λίθιναι ὑδρίαι⸃ ἓξ ⸂κατὰ τὸν καθαρισμὸν τῶν Ἰουδαίων κείμεναι⸃, χωροῦσαι ἀνὰ μετρητὰς δύο ἢ τρεῖς.

verses.restored: Jesus says to them, Fill the jars with water. They filled them up to the top.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto them, Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim.

modern.text: Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim.

original.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Γεμίσατε τὰς ὑδρίας ὕδατος· καὶ ἐγέμισαν αὐτὰς ἕως ἄνω.

verses.restored: He says to them, Draw now and carry to the steward of the feast. They carried it.

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. And they bare it.

modern.text: “Now draw some out,” He said, “and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so,

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἀντλήσατε νῦν καὶ φέρετε τῷ ἀρχιτρικλίνῳ· ⸂οἱ δὲ⸃ ἤνεγκαν.

verses.restored: When the steward of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know from where it was, though the servants who had drawn the water knew, the steward calls the bridegroom,

familiar.text: When the ruler of the feast had tasted the water that was made wine, and knew not whence it was: (but the servants which drew the water knew;) the governor of the feast called the bridegroom,

modern.text: and the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine. He did not know where it was from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. Then he called the bridegroom aside

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἐγεύσατο ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος τὸ ὕδωρ οἶνον γεγενημένον, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει πόθεν ἐστίν, οἱ δὲ διάκονοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ ἠντληκότες τὸ ὕδωρ, φωνεῖ τὸν νυμφίον ὁ ἀρχιτρίκλινος

verses.restored: and says to him, Every person sets out the beautiful/good wine first, and when they have drunk freely, the lesser; you have kept the beautiful/good wine until now.

familiar.text: And saith unto him, Every man at the beginning doth set forth good wine; and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse: but thou hast kept the good wine until now.

modern.text: and said, “Everyone serves the fine wine first, and then the cheap wine after the guests are drunk. But you have saved the fine wine until now!”

original.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Πᾶς ἄνθρωπος πρῶτον τὸν καλὸν οἶνον τίθησιν, καὶ ὅταν ⸀μεθυσθῶσιν τὸν ἐλάσσω· σὺ τετήρηκας τὸν καλὸν οἶνον ἕως ἄρτι.

verses.restored: This beginning of signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples trusted into him.

familiar.text: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

modern.text: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him. Jesus Cleanses the Temple (Matthew 21:12–17; Mark 11:15–19; Luke 19:45–48)

original.text: ταύτην ⸀ἐποίησεν ἀρχὴν τῶν σημείων ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἐφανέρωσεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: After this he went down to Capernaum, he and his mother, brothers, and disciples, and they remained there not many days.

familiar.text: After this he went down to Capernaum, he, and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples: and they continued there not many days.

modern.text: After this, He went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed there a few days.

original.text: Μετὰ τοῦτο κατέβη εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ αὐτὸς καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ⸀ἀδελφοὶ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκεῖ ἔμειναν οὐ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.

verses.restored: The Passover of the Judeans was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,

modern.text: When the Jewish Passover was near, Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγγὺς ἦν τὸ πάσχα τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: He found in the temple those selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and the money-changers seated.

familiar.text: And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:

modern.text: In the temple courts He found men selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers seated at their tables.

original.text: καὶ εὗρεν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τοὺς πωλοῦντας βόας καὶ πρόβατα καὶ περιστερὰς καὶ τοὺς κερματιστὰς καθημένους,

verses.restored: Making a whip from cords, he drove all out of the temple, both sheep and cattle; he poured out the coins of the money-changers and overturned the tables.

familiar.text: And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;

modern.text: So He made a whip out of cords and drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle. He poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables.

original.text: καὶ ποιήσας φραγέλλιον ἐκ σχοινίων πάντας ἐξέβαλεν ἐκ τοῦ ἱεροῦ τά τε πρόβατα καὶ τοὺς βόας, καὶ τῶν κολλυβιστῶν ἐξέχεεν ⸂τὰ κέρματα⸃ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας ⸀ἀνέστρεψεν,

verses.restored: To those selling doves he said, Take these things from here; do not make my Father's house a house of marketplace/trade.

familiar.text: And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.

modern.text: To those selling doves He said, “Get these out of here! How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!”

original.text: καὶ τοῖς τὰς περιστερὰς πωλοῦσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ταῦτα ἐντεῦθεν, μὴ ποιεῖτε τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου οἶκον ἐμπορίου.

verses.restored: His disciples remembered that it is written, Zeal for your house will consume me.

familiar.text: And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.

modern.text: His disciples remembered that it is written: “Zeal for Your house will consume Me.”

original.text: ⸀ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι γεγραμμένον ἐστίν· Ὁ ζῆλος τοῦ οἴκου σου καταφάγεταί με.

verses.restored: Therefore the Judeans answered and said to him, What sign do you show us, since you do these things?

familiar.text: Then answered the Jews and said unto him, What sign shewest thou unto us, seeing that thou doest these things?

modern.text: On account of this, the Jews demanded, “What sign can You show us to prove Your authority to do these things?”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Τί σημεῖον δεικνύεις ἡμῖν, ὅτι ταῦτα ποιεῖς;

verses.restored: Jesus answered and said to them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it.

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.

modern.text: Jesus answered, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The Judeans said, This temple was built in forty-six years, and you will raise it in three days?

familiar.text: Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days?

modern.text: “This temple took forty-six years to build,” the Jews replied, “and You are going to raise it up in three days?”

original.text: εἶπαν οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι· Τεσσεράκοντα καὶ ἓξ ἔτεσιν οἰκοδομήθη ὁ ναὸς οὗτος, καὶ σὺ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερεῖς αὐτόν;

verses.restored: But he was speaking about the temple of his body.

familiar.text: But he spake of the temple of his body.

modern.text: But Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body.

original.text: ἐκεῖνος δὲ ἔλεγεν περὶ τοῦ ναοῦ τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When therefore he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they trusted the Scripture and the word Jesus had spoken.

familiar.text: When therefore he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this unto them; and they believed the scripture, and the word which Jesus had said.

modern.text: After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

original.text: ὅτε οὖν ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐμνήσθησαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τοῦτο ἔλεγεν, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν τῇ γραφῇ καὶ τῷ λόγῳ ⸀ὃν εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: While he was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many trusted into his name, beholding the signs he was doing.

familiar.text: Now when he was in Jerusalem at the passover, in the feast day, many believed in his name, when they saw the miracles which he did.

modern.text: While He was in Jerusalem at the Passover Feast, many people saw the signs He was doing and believed in His name.

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἦν ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν τῷ πάσχα ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ, πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, θεωροῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐποίει·

verses.restored: But Jesus himself was not entrusting himself to them, because he knew all people,

familiar.text: But Jesus did not commit himself unto them, because he knew all men,

modern.text: But Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all.

original.text: αὐτὸς ⸀δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκ ἐπίστευεν ⸀αὑτὸν αὐτοῖς διὰ τὸ αὐτὸν γινώσκειν πάντας

verses.restored: and because he had no need that anyone should bear witness concerning a human, for he himself knew what was in the human.

familiar.text: And needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

modern.text: He did not need any testimony about man, for He knew what was in a man.

original.text: καὶ ὅτι οὐ χρείαν εἶχεν ἵνα τις μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, αὐτὸς γὰρ ἐγίνωσκεν τί ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ.
